0.long_answer: Persistent Müllerian duct syndrome (PMDS) is a congenital disorder that occurs in genetically male (46,XY) individuals due to abnormal anti-Müllerian hormone (AMH) signaling. Normally, AMH is secreted by the Sertoli cells in the testes during early embryonic development to trigger the regression of the Müllerian ducts, which would otherwise develop into female reproductive organs. In PMDS, either a deficiency in the hormone or a defect in its receptor prevents this regression, leading to the retention of a uterus, fallopian tubes, and upper vaginal structures in an otherwise typically male individual. Historically, this condition was classified as a form of pseudohermaphroditism because of the coexistence of male chromosomal and gonadal characteristics with the presence of female internal reproductive structures.
